PASS but item_text mapping (dsi_1..dsi_23) is a reconstruction, not a source-confirmed key. The paper (Alexander 2017, PeerJ, 10.7717/peerj.3034) states it used the DSI's Emotional Reactivity (11 items) and Emotional Cutoff (12 items) subscales = 23 items, matching the live item count exactly (Step 3b instrument-mismatch check: table name says generic 'dsi' but live data is actually only these two of the DSI's four subscales, not the full 43-item DSI-R -- confirmed via PeerJ's own supplementary raw-data file (peerj-05-3034-s001.xlsx, fetched via Europe PMC's supplementaryFiles zip endpoint), whose Sheet2 codebook lists only DSI_1..DSI_23 alongside ECR/EAS/Antifat/Binge_EA columns, no other DSI items). Full 43-item verbatim text and subscale composition (with reverse-scoring key) was recovered from the original instrument's published Appendix (Skowron & Friedlander, 1998, Journal of Counseling Psychology, appendix reproduced at https://montessori.org.au/sites/default/files/downloads/downloads/EC198LauraFloresShawWorkshopHandout.pdf). Neither the paper nor its supplementary files disclose the exact dsi_1..dsi_23 ordering used on the actual administered survey. dsi_N was mapped to the original 43-item Appendix by taking the 23 Emotional-Reactivity + Emotional-Cutoff items in their original ascending Appendix item-number order (deleting the 20 I-Position/Fusion-with-Others items and preserving relative order of the rest) -- a defensible but unconfirmed assumption; if the study instead grouped items by subscale block or used a different/randomised order, the dsi_N-to-item_text mapping in this file would be wrong despite passing validate_items.R (which only checks the item/resp value sets, not content-to-code alignment).

CSE1-CSE12 assumed to map 1:1 onto the original scale's numbered order 1-12 (not independently confirmed against the German instrument).
